originality.rationale: Claim and implication comparison: original 2026 spectral synthesis article defines the indicator Fourier algebra norm but its exact parabola formulas use affine transitivity of a single quadratic graph. Published two-opposite-parabola projection uses intersecting curves and a signed Gauss character sum, different from disjoint vertical lifts; neither its formula nor parameter specialization produces the arbitrary-H transfer. The cubic-fold result has different dimension, q^2 points versus 2q for the two-sheet case, and a one-or-two-root Fourier kernel; sharing the cosecant factor does not imply the stated norm or energy. Same geometrical translates occur in a line-cover theorem, but it proves covering numbers, not analytic norms. The distinct all-fiber Fourier spectrum and additive-energy statement is not implied by the inspected work. Older indexed or unindexed equivalent identities remain possible.
residual_risks: An earlier Fourier algebra/idempotent norm computation for quadratic graphs with vertical fibers may be unindexed or in a source under another title.

The general absolute-kernel factorization is elementary once its support is recognized; its standalone novelty/value rests on the complete family reduction, exact two-sheet characteristic formula, energy and zeros together, not on claiming a new Gaussian-sum lemma.
